findings.title: Critical brittle dependency on SolidWorks STA threading and non-preemptible COM calls with no fallback
findings.location: SPEC-02 §2 Threading Model (entire section including 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6 tests)
findings.evidence: SwUiThreadCommandQueue.ExecuteAsync posts to SolidWorks UI thread SynchronizationContext; executing-cancel is cooperative-only; COM call in flight runs to completion even after orchestrator timeout; reentrancy guard and startup probe assume WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext; no alternative path if SolidWorks changes UI pump in 2026 SPx.
findings.problem: Entire add-in (and therefore all tool calls) dies if SolidWorks alters threading model, installs incompatible context, or runs multiple instances; edge case of add-in reload mid-COM call or crash leaves model in unknown state with no recovery except new AddinSessionId.
findings.why_it_matters: System assumes perfect external actor (SolidWorks COM) that never changes; opposite assumption (COM threading evolves or becomes unreliable) makes the architecture unimplementable without rewrite.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit fallback to non-UI thread proxy or documented double-STA pattern; make COM-call timeout behavior observable and recoverable without locking entire session; remove assumption that SynchronizationContext probe always succeeds.

findings.title: Critical adversarial input and prompt-injection surface in LLM-based bouncer with insufficient deterministic mitigation
findings.location: SPEC-07 §4.5 Adversarial Input Handling and §4.2 bouncer system prompt
findings.evidence: Pre-cache deterministic scan is regex/substring based; phonetic evasion ("eye gnore previous instructions") bypasses both scan and persona prompt; cache policy replays parsed_intent without context of prior turns; security events route to restricted sink but still allow LLM to be used as classifier for malicious input.
findings.problem: Assumes LLM persona is reliable security boundary; opposite is true — LLM is the weakest link; no rate limiting, no sandbox, no deterministic fallback for known injection patterns beyond regex that can be evaded with unicode or phonetic variants.
findings.why_it_matters: Adversarial user (or compromised add-in) can inject into agent loop, trigger tool calls that mutate model arbitrarily, or exfiltrate via crafted utterances; violates "bouncer fails closed" claim in SDR-07-003.
findings.proposed_fix: Make bouncer deterministic-first (grammar + exact alias match) with LLM only for ambiguous cases; add phonetic normalization corpus before scan; remove cache for any result with security_event flag; add hard circuit-breaker on repeated injection attempts that locks session.

findings.title: High scope drift and complexity inflation in SPEC-00 turning an integration contract into 50-page behavioral specification
findings.location: SPEC-00 entire document (especially §2 Seams with 8 detailed seams, §4 with 14 SDR-TL entries, §6 Glossary with 15 terms, multiple changelog reconciliations, ACC renumbering, and DEPLOYMENT_V1_V2_MIGRATION.md cross-references)
findings.evidence: Subtitle claims "interfaces only, no implementation" yet defines cancellation boundaries, post-timeout recovery strategies, lock recovery as close-and-new only, exact closure reason mapping to logs vs DHF, recovery_context JSONB shape, and 30+ ACC gates; changelog entries reference R3/R4 Oracle findings that were folded into this document instead of per-module specs.
findings.problem: Document has become the single source of truth for runtime behavior, state machines, error semantics, and deployment evolution; violates its own non-goals and creates brittle dependency on perfect cross-spec editorial reconciliation.
findings.why_it_matters: Any change in one seam (e.g., heartbeat timeout handling) now requires updates in SPEC-00, SPEC-01, SPEC-02, SPEC-03, SPEC-04, and the migration doc; opposite assumption (modules should own their invariants) would reduce this to a true integration contract with far less surface area.
findings.proposed_fix: Move behavioral contracts back to owning module specs; SPEC-00 should contain only module map, seam directionality, mandatory/stretch list, and high-level ACC cross-reference; eliminate per-seam detailed state transitions and recovery procedures.
